Tailwind v4 no-op utility classes: this project pins tailwindcss ^4.1.8 and installs NO scrollbar plugin, so the class scrollbar-none generates NO CSS at all - it silently does nothing. Hide a native scrollbar track with the arbitrary form [scrollbar-width:none] (Firefox) plus [&::-webkit-scrollbar]:hidden (WebKit/Blink), which need no plugin. DIR-086 fixed this in EducationStep.jsx:469, WorkHistoryStep.jsx:285 and DashboardHomepage.jsx:1179, and a post-certification sweep found one last occurrence at src/components/JobsListings/JobSearchBar.jsx:188 (flagged to the Lead, NOT applied because DIR-086 was already frozen). GENERAL RULE: before trusting any utility class, confirm its plugin/dependency actually exists in package.json.

DUPLICATE-WAKE STORM (bridge v3.0.0, observed on DIR-086): the lead-side watcher re-dispatches a dev wake on EVERY directive transition without checking whether the directive is already TERMINAL. DIR-086 produced SIX wake files - one recon (11:59:14), one PLAN (12:07:59), TWO ACT wakes at plan-approval (12:08:43 and 12:08:45), one at 12:18:19, and one at 12:21:07 rendered from an EVIDENCE_SUBMITTED snapshot. The 12:21:07 wake still carried 'Status: IN_PROGRESS' in its body even though the directive had reached APPROVED_FROZEN three seconds later, so the templated prompt is generated from a stale snapshot. HANDLING RULE for the developer: on receiving a wake, FIRST read the live directive JSON status - if it is APPROVED_FROZEN (or any terminal state) and HEAD matches the freeze hash with zero source drift, the wake is a duplicate; acknowledge it with bridge ack --role dev --id <wakeId> (idempotent) and do NOT re-run the gate suite, re-submit evidence, or re-apply changes, because that is pure noise against a certified baseline. Only genuine work in a re-delivered wake is one whose live status is ISSUED or IN_PROGRESS with a real unapplied delta.

CUBA SEMANTIC TOKENS ARE SOLID BADGES, NOT TINTS - do not remap light colour tints onto --cuba-pill-* tokens. Verified values in src/styles/cuba-tokens.css: --cuba-pill-success-fill = #1a7f37 (SOLID green) and --cuba-pill-success-ink = #ffffff (WHITE). So mapping a light tint like bg-green-50 onto --cuba-pill-success-fill would turn a subtle wash into a solid block, and mapping text-green-700 onto --cuba-pill-success-ink would make dark text white. Light tints must use the -soft variants (--cuba-success-soft, --cuba-info-soft, --cuba-warning-soft, --cuba-danger-soft), which are rgba at ~0.12 alpha. Neutral structural shades DO map 1:1 and are safe to automate: slate-50 to --cuba-canvas (#f4f5f9), slate-200 to --cuba-line (#dfe3ee), slate-300 to --cuba-line-strong (#c6ccdc), slate-500/600 to --cuba-ink-subtle (#626a7d), slate-700 to --cuba-ink-muted (#4a5163), slate-800/900 to --cuba-ink (#10121a), light text to --cuba-ink-inverse (#f7f8fc). ALSO: the Cuba shadow tokens are SIZES (--cuba-shadow-sm/md/lg/xl) while shadow-slate-200 sets a shadow COLOUR, so that one must never be swapped mechanically. DIR-088 tokenised only the neutral half (1072 substitutions across 32 files) for exactly these reasons; the 1179 semantic state colours need per-surface visual verification.
